title: Ani-One Asia Streams Magical Girl Raising Project restart Anime
content:
Ani-One Asia describes the anime:

Chosen by the "Land of Magic" that exists hidden from the human world, girls are granted unique powers to become magical girls. Among them is Pechka, who uses the magic to "make food delicious." Alongside 16 other unfamiliar, highly distinct magical girls, she is forced to participate in a mysterious virtual game. What was supposed to be a safe training exercise to enhance their magical abilities turns out to be the beginning of an engineered nightmare, a forbidden trial. It marks the restart of a new " Magical Girl Raising Project ."

The anime anime debuted in Japan on Monday late at night at 2:00 a.m. (effectively Tuesday).

The anime stars:

• Yoshino Nanjō as Pfle

• Reina Kondo as Shadow Gale

• Fairouz Ai as Masked Wonder

• Honoka Inoue as Pechka

• Jenya as Nonako Miyokata

• M.A.O as Rionetta

• Mariya Ise as Clantail

• Maaya Uchida as Magical Daisy

• Hime Sawada as Nokko-chan

• Akari Kitō as @Meow-Meow

• Sayumi Suzushiro as Genopsyko Yumenoshima

• Ami Koshimizu as Akane

• Shiori Mikami as Melville

• Maria Naganawa as Cherna Mouse

• Miyu Tomita as Detec Bell

• Aoi Yūki as Lapis Lazuline

• Megumi Han as Keek

Nao Tōyama returns from the original anime as Snow White.

Hiroyuki Hashimoto returns from the first Magical Girl Raising Project anime as the director. Takao Yoshioka is returning to write the script. Masako Itou ( Magical Girl Raising Project SD character designer) is designing the characters for the new anime based on original designs by Maruino . Satoki Iida is returning as sound director. Synergy SP is the new animation studio, replacing Lerche that animated the previous Magical Girl Raising Project anime. Minori Chihara performs the anime's opening theme song "No tears here." Daisy×Daisy performs the ending theme song "ReMind."

The first 12-episode Magical Girl Raising Project anime premiered in Japan on the AT-X channel in October 2016.

Endō's Mahō Shōjo Ikusei Keikaku light novel series is set in a world where a social game called The Magical G irl Raising Project allows one in tens of thousands of people to be a "magical girl" — possessing extraordinary physical capabilities and looks, as well as special magical powers that set them apart from the rest of the human race. But one day, in a district containing 16 magical girls, the administration announces that it must halve the number of magical girls to solve the problem of magical energy. At first, the 16 magical girls race to collect more "magical candy" than their competitors, but the rules quickly become twisted, and it quickly becomes a murderous battle for survival among them.

Endō launched the original light novel series through Takarajimasha 's Kono Light Novel ga Sugoi! Bunko imprint in June 2012, and Takarajimasha published the 18th volume in November 2023. The second and third light novel volumes, published in November and December 2012, cover the "Restart" arc. Yen Press began publishing the novel series in English in June 2017.

Nori-Senbei launched the manga adaptation of the "Restart" arc in Kadokawa 's Monthly Comp Ace magazine in 2016, and Kadokawa published one volume in September 2016.

title: Mackenyu Will Appear at London MCM Comic Con in October
content:
The MCM London Comic Con has announced on its X/Twitter feed that the actor Mackenyu , who plays Roronoa Zoro in the live-action One Piece webseries, will appear at the event which runs from Friday October 23 to Sunday October 25. The venue is London's ExCel Centre.

Mackenyu will appear on the Saturday and Sunday. He will participate in autograph and photo sessions ( details ), as well as a panel on the Sunday.

As well as Roronoa Zoro in the live-action One Piece webseries, Mackenyu plays Arata Wataya in the live-action Chihayafuru films, Seiya in the live-action Knights of the Zodiac film and Enishi in the live-action film Rurouni Kenshin Saishūshō The Final .

The following anime-related events are scheduled at October's MCM London Comic Con:

Friday

5 p.m. to 5.45 p.m. - "Getting Supernatural with DanDaDan" on the Live Stage, a panel featuring the dub actors A.J. Beckles (Okarun) and Kari Wahlgren (Granny Seiko).

Sunday

1.30 p.m. - Mackenyu Panel on the main stage. The panel is described as follows: "Join Mackenyu as he talks about bringing one of anime's most iconic characters to life, the training and preparation behind Zoro's legendary swordsmanship, working on the Netflix series, and his journey as an actor."

3 p.m. to 3.45 p.m. - Anime Limited Industry Panel featuring Andy Hanley and Tomi Murphy.

4 p.m. to 4.45 p.m. - Hunting Monsters with Jujutsu Kaisen on the Live Stage featuring the dub actors Anne Yatco (Nobara Kugisaki), David Vincent (Kento Nanami) and Allegra Clark (Kazumi Miwa, Maki Zenin).

title: Pokémon Permanently Banned An Episode That Was Deemed Too Dangerous to Air, & It Was Pikachu’s Fault
content:
There are plenty of ways an episode of Pokémon can become memorable. Maybe Ash catches a new Pokémon, Team Rocket gets blasted off again, or Pikachu finds himself in the middle of another adventure that somehow goes completely off the rails. But every once in a while, an episode becomes famous for something nobody involved could have expected. One particular installment of the Pokémon anime managed to do exactly that, becoming so infamous that it was pulled from circulation and never officially aired again. For a franchise that has produced more than a thousand episodes, that’s quite a distinction.

The strange part is that this wasn’t supposed to be some controversial episode. There was no shocking storyline, no particularly dangerous Pokémon, and certainly no plan to make television history. It was just another colorful episode of one of the biggest anime series in the world. Then something happened during the broadcast that sent viewers to hospitals, forced the show off the air temporarily, and changed how animation handled certain visual effects. It’s a historic event that the community should be aware of.

Electric Soldier Porygon Caused a Pokémon Television Disaster

The episode was Electric Soldier Porygon , which aired in Japan on December 16, 1997. Ah, the 1990s—such a great time for cartoons and anime. However, this particular night would prove to be an eclipse in that space. During a battle sequence, Pikachu gets serious and fires an electric attack that produces a burst of rapidly alternating red and blue flashes. For some viewers, particularly those susceptible to photosensitive reactions, the effect had a negative impact on their physical health. Sources claimed that at least 600 children were reported to have experienced symptoms including seizures, headaches, dizziness, and nausea, with many taken to hospitals following the broadcast.

The reaction was widespread and immediate enough to become a major news story in Japan. Pokémon was temporarily taken off the air while the circumstances surrounding the broadcast were investigated. And of course, the episode was never officially shown again. It also never received an official international broadcast. Like an urban myth, it quickly became an episode that existed but that viewers are never supposed to see.

Pikachu Walked Away While Porygon Practically Disappeared

The consequences didn’t end with the episode being pulled. The entire incident became an important example of the risks associated with rapidly flashing images on television—and an unfortunate, painful reminder. TV stations were put on notice, particularly when it came to programming aimed at children. Animation studios and broadcasters became more careful about how those effects were used. And Pokémon changed its production and broadcast practices in response to what had happened.

There is also an unfortunate element of blame buried in all of this. The episode has Porygon’s name right there in the title, but Porygon didn’t directly produce the effect that caused the problem. Pikachu was the one who launched the attack. Porygon just happened to be standing nearby when television history took a very unpleasant turn. So, Porygon shouldn’t be the one to take the rap.

For fans, though, one of the other unfortunate results is what happened to Porygon afterward. The Pokémon most closely associated with the episode effectively disappeared from the anime’s regular adventures, despite not actually producing the flashing effect. Pikachu, meanwhile, remained exactly where you would expect him to be. He was still front and center, becoming even more recognizable as the face of the franchise. Even if new Pokémon appear on a regular basis, it’s still quite sad.

That makes the whole episode an especially odd chapter in Pokémon history. One moment, Electric Soldier Porygon was simply another episode on the schedule. The next, it had become something the series could never really put back on television. And Porygon? Well, Porygon learned the hard way that sometimes being the Pokémon in the title is not the same thing as being the Pokémon who caused the trouble.

title: Skull Dragon's Precious Daughter Anime Unveils 1st Promo Video, Main Cast, 2027 Debut
content:
Kadokawa revealed the first main promotional video, main visual, main cast members, and 2027 debut for the television anime of Ichi Yukishiro 's Skull Dragon's Precious Daughter ( Hone Dragon no Manamusume ) manga, on Thursday.

The anime will star:

Kana Hanazawa as Eve, a girl abandoned in the Forest of Scraps

Kazuhiko Inoue as Nemu, the Skull Dragon who raised Eve

In the Forest of Scraps, a place where all manner of things are discarded, an old dragon sleeps away his final days—that is, until an abandoned child suddenly appears before him. The tiny human is Eve, and despite being only five years of age, she has somehow endured the many dangers that surround them. In an act of pity, the dragon decides to raise her as his own...but his time is still running out. After five years together, he takes his last breath, leaving his precious daughter on her own. Little does the dragon know, Eve is capable of more than he realizes, and their reunion may be sooner than he thinks… Hoping to improve Eve's control over her magical abilities before his resurrected body gives out, the skull dragon sets out on an adventure with his reckless human daughter—but who knows what kind of trouble awaits them?

Kuniyasu Nishina ( Oshi no Ko , Blue Period , 86 episode director) is directing the anime at Dōga Kōbō . Yuka Yamada ( Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid S , Nina the Starry Bride , Tokyo Mew Mew New ) is in charge of the series scripts, and Tomoya Atsumi ( Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba , Love Live! Nijigasaki High School Idol Club , The Quintessential Quintuplets episode key animator) is designing the characters. Kusanagi 's Daiki Kuribayashi ( 7th Time Loop: The Villainess Enjoys a Carefree Life , Dragon Ball Super: Broly film) and Yūki Hatakeyama ( Black Butler: Emerald Witch Arc , One Piece Film Gold ) are in charge of background art.

Yukishiro launched the manga on Mag Garden 's Mag Comi website in 2020. Mag Garden published the manga's sixth compiled book volume in August 2025. Seven Seas will publish the sixth volume in English on December 1. The manga went on hiatus in July and will return in spring next year.

title: Horror Collector Anime Adds 3 Cast Members
content:
The official website for the television anime of Midori Satō 's Horror Collector ( Kyōfu Collector ) novel series revealed three new cast members for the anime on Thursday. The new cast members include:

Sae Hiratsuka as Momo

Ryōta Ōsaka as Raita

Hana Hishikawa as Sachiko Konno

The anime's staff also revealed the anime's guest cast for the first three episodes. Yōko Hikasa voices Urban Legend Woman in the first episode. Sumire Uesaka voices high schooler Seira Takada in the second episode. Yūma Uchida voices magazine journalist Takaaki Saitō in the third episode.

Previously announced cast members include:

Hiiro Ishibashi as Fushigi Senno

Jun Fukuyama as Jimmy

Saori Hayami as Himitsu

Nobuhiko Okamoto as Blue Umbrella Man

The anime will debut on NHK on October 10. Crunchyroll will stream the anime as it airs in Japan.

Yuki Inaba ( KamiKatsu: Working for God in a Godless World , Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World season 2) is directing the anime at Studio Palette , and is also in charge of series composition. Kaori Yoshikawa ( KamiKatsu: Working for God in a Godless World , Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World season 2) is designing the characters. Masato Kōda is composing the music. Tetsuya Gunji is the audio director.

Yen Press is releasing the novel series and Niko Yuki 's manga adaptation in English for its "JY for Kids" middle-grade imprint, and it describes the story:

The internet is full of creepypastas, cryptid sightings, tales of paranormal activity, and unsolved disappearances. These are mostly rumors and pranks fueled by trolls—entertainment. But the unlucky few learn the hard way that some legends are true. Many of these unfortunate souls are doomed, but their luck may change if they cross paths with the boy in the red hood. He roams from town to town and appears wherever strange things occur. Is he a light in the dark? Or living proof that monsters are all too real...?

Sato writes the novels, Norio Tsuruta is the supervisor, and Yon draws the art for the novel series. Kadokawa started releasing the novel series in June 2015, and published the 29th volume on Wednesday.

Yuki's manga adaptation ran in Kadokawa 's Monthly Comic Gene magazine in 2021-2022. Kadokawa published the manga adaptation in one volume in March 2022.

Yen Press published the sixth novel volume in May 2025, and published the manga in one volume in May 2025.

title: Hideaki Anno, Yutaka Izubuchi Co-Direct Yamato √2199 Film at I.G, Khara
content:
A website opened on Tuesday to announce that Hideaki Anno and Yutaka Izubuchi are directing the feature-length anime film Cosmoship Yamato √2199 at Production I.G and Studio Khara . (The film's Japanese title uses the same "Uchū Senkan" prefix previously also translated as "Space Battleship" or "Space Cruiser," and the √ symbol is pronounced "Root.")

The project also credits Anno for planning with Production I.G founder Mitsuhisa Ishikawa , as the production executive producer, and for design works with Izubuchi. "Shin Office Academy " is presenting the project.

The website quotes Anno ("a huge Yamato fan since the second year of junior high school"): "I want to keep making Yamato not only to fulfill a childhood dream, but also to imbue our prayers and wishes for the next generation and our own. It is with that resolve that we produce this."

Anno, arguably best known for co-creating Neon Genesis Evangelion and working on the Shin Godzilla , Shin Ultraman , and Shin Kamen Rider films, has frequently cited Yamato as inspiring his interest in anime. He previously planned the opening sequence to the Space Battleship Yamato 2199 series. Anno stated in a comment about the 50th anniversary project that he has been a fan of the franchise for 49 years, since his second year in middle school. He added that he did not think he would be the same person he is today without the franchise . He reminisced about how he missed the first episode when it was first broadcast, but how he watched the second through final episode, sacrificing even watching Great Mazinger and running home after cram school to do so.

Anno joined Production I.G 's board of directors on August 21, 2025.

The original Yamato anime follows the voyages of the World War II battleship Yamato after it is resurrected as a space-faring ship to fend off alien threats to Earth. The first television series premiered in October of 1974. The first animated film then opened in 1977 and earned 2.1 billion yen (about US$23 million) at the box office. The anime franchise later garnered a record instantaneous television rating of 50% in 1978.

Yamato yo Towa ni: Rebel 3199 (Be Forever Yamato: Rebel 3199), the current project in the Space Battleship Yamato 2199 remakes, is opening as seven films, beginning with the first film "Kuro no Shinryaku" (Dark Invasion) in July 2024. The final film will open in Japan on October 30.

The first television series premiered in October of 1974. The first animated film then opened in 1977 and earned 2.1 billion yen (about US$23 million) at the box office. The anime franchise later garnered a record instantaneous television rating of 50% in 1978.

Yamato yo Towa ni: Rebel 3199 (Be Forever Yamato: Rebel 3199), the current project in the Space Battleship Yamato 2199 remakes, is opening as seven films, beginning with the first film "Kuro no Shinryaku" (Dark Invasion) in July 2024. The final film will open in Japan on October 30.

title: Crunchyroll Manga App Expands to U.K., Ireland, South Asia, ANZ
content:
Crunchyroll also announced that it will be "easily accessible" in a new dedicated anime hub for the PlayStation 5 console that will launch next spring. The anime space on the console will also include anime games and anime-inspired games.

The Crunchyroll Manga app launched on iOS and Android devices in the United States and Canada in October 2025. The ad-free app is separate from the main Crunchyroll streaming service.

Crunchyroll is discontinuing its main app on the Nintendo Switch on October 30. Crunchyroll is still available on Xbox and PlayStation , as well as on mobile devices, media players, Smart TVs and TVs, service providers, and via web browsers.

Crunchyroll increased the prices for all of its subscription tiers in the U.S. in February, and Crunchyroll halted free ad-supported streaming on its service last December.

title: The Seven Knights of the Marronnier Kingdom Anime Unveils More Cast
content:
The official website for the television anime of Nao Iwamoto 's Marronnier Ōkoku no Shichinin no Kishi ( The Seven Knights of the Marronnier Kingdom ) manga announced three more cast members for the anime on Thursday:

Natsuki Hanae as Justice, a knight of the Marronnier Kingdom and Hugo's nephew

Mitsuki Saiga as Zoe, Justice's adjutant

Miyuri Shimabukuro as Colette, the daughter of the kingdom's head chef

The fantasy romance manga centers on seven brothers who are knights of the Marronnier Kingdom. The kingdom lies in the center of a group of eight kingdoms, and each brother is dispatched to a different kingdom as ambassadors, to go on an adventure to find their fated partner.

The anime stars:

• Kengo Takanashi as Nemukunai (Insomniac)

• Makoto Tanikawa as Hakuai (Fraternity)

• Haruki Ishiya as Atsugariya (Feverish)

• Satoshi Inomata as Samugariya (Chilly)

• Kiyoto Mizuno as Kemono Tsukai (Beast-Tamer)

• Taishi Murata as Tsurugi Jiman (Swordsman)

• Reiji Kawashima as Harapeko (Hungry)

• Akeno Watanabe as Baribara

• Show Hayami as Narrator

Kiyoko Sayama ( Skip Beat! , Vampire Knight , To Your Eternity seasons 2-3) is directing the anime at J.C. Staff . Shinzō Fujita ( To Your Eternity seasons 1-3, The World Is Still Beautiful ) is both writing and overseeing the series scripts. Yuriko Maeda (chief animation director for Requiem of the Rose King , One Punch Man TV 2 ) is designing the characters, Yoshiaki Fujisawa ( Apocalypse Hotel , Land of the Lustrous , Love Live! School idol project ) is composing the music, and Jin Aketagawa ( Dr. Stone , Fire Force ) is the sound director.

The anime premiered on the NHK Educational channel on October 3 at 6:25 p.m. JST (5:25 a.m. EDT). Amazon Prime Video is streaming the anime, and is also streaming an English dub .

Viz Media licensed the manga on October 1 and uploaded the first two chapters digitally on the same day.

The manga launched in Shogakukan 's Flowers magazine in 2016. Shogakukan shipped the 11th volume on June 10. The manga topped the list of manga for female readers in the 2018 edition of Takarajimasha 's Kono Manga ga Sugoi! (This Manga Is Amazing!) guidebook.

title: 20 Years Later, There’s Still No Shonen Jump Anime That Deserves a Reboot More
content:
When it comes to Shonen action and drama, Weekly Shonen Jump always grabs the spotlight, and this has been the case for many decades now. Established in 1968, it eventually became the best-selling manga magazine of all time. A lot of its popularity is thanks to Dragon Ball, One Piece, and many other Shonen classics that kept the magazine running. However, while several of these classics received anime, not all of them got the adaptations they deserve. While the 2000s were a golden era for Shonen fans, many incredible anime suffered from poor pacing and cancellations. This also includes Katekyo Hitman Reborn, a classic Shonen action written and illustrated by Akira Amano.

This action comedy began serialization in 2004 and reached its finale in 2012 with 42 manga volumes. The series followed several plot lines and featured lovable characters throughout its run, which is all the more reason it’s a favorite among fans even now. The anime premiered on October 7th, 2006, which further helped the manga gain more popularity. However, despite having an exceptional story and power system, the anime couldn’t stand the test of time due to several issues. Now that the anime is commemorating its 20th anniversary today, it’s evident that it needs a reboot to adapt the entire story with better animation and pacing.

Katekyo Hitman Reborn Anime Was Cancelled Before It Could Adapt the Entire Story

The biggest flaw with long-running, weekly anime was that it would always catch up with the manga. Many Weekly Shonen Jump series followed the same pattern, and as a result, they would face the same issues as well. The anime would be released at least a couple of years after the manga debut, and both versions of the story would be released weekly. Manga chapters are considerably shorter, while the anime needs to adapt at least more than one chapter per episode. There’s no question as to why the anime would end up facing pacing issues. This is also the reason why many anime leaned towards having so many filler episodes.

However, despite all that, some of them would still be unable to continue on. This even includes a hit classic like Bleach, which adapted the final arc ten years after the original anime ended. As for Katekyo Hitman Reborn , the anime released more than 200 episodes, but it never returned with a sequel. While the series was a hit during its serialization, it faced a decline in popularity as sales became lower for Blu-rays and merchandise. This also discouraged the studio from continuing the anime. However, at this point, a reboot that will adapt the manga with better animation, pacing, and a seasonal schedule is more needed than the continuation of the original anime.

Katekyu Hitman Reborn Has Major Plans For the 20th Anniversary

title: Walking Home with You Anime Reveals Visual, April 2027 Premiere
content:
Walking Home with You anime revealed a new visual along with an April 2027 premiere date on Wednesday. No further details on the studio, staff, or cast were announced as of this writing.

Mai Matsuda writes and illustrates the manga which the anime is based on. Futabasha’s Manga Action magazine has been serializing the title since 2023. Omoi is releasing it in English, describing the series as follows:

A fresh coming-of-age romantic comedy about taking the long way home, from Mai Matsuda, creator of Hikaru in the Light! Shun was the star of his middle school’s soccer team, until an injury forced him to give up on his dream. Now in high school, he’s adrift, with no real interests or passions … until he meets his oddball upperclassman Naoki. She ropes him into joining her unofficial “Hyper-Epic Heading Home Club,” a club with only one member dedicated to turning every walk home into an adventure. As Shun follows Naoki through her flights of fancy in search of elaborate detours, secret treasures, and anything else that catches her attention, can the Heading Home Club bring color back to his drab everyday life?

A commemorative illustration from Matsuda was also unveiled:
